newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Activists on secret trip to disputed islands.
newsitem.headline: Activists on secret trip to disputed islands.

text.p: Taiwan media reported on Tuesday a fresh attempt by activists to sail to a disputed Japanese-held archipelago in the East China Sea, timed for Hong Kong's handover to China.

Ching Chieh-shou, a Taipei County councillor, and 15 others, including six journalists, set off late on Monday by fishing boat to the island chain, known in Chinese as the Diaoyus and in Japanese as the Senkakus, state-funded Central News Agency said.
There was no immediate confirmation of the voyage.
The agency said the group was expected to approach the Diaoyu archipelago by midnight Monday as Britain handed Hong Kong back to China, ending 156 years of British colonial rule.
Taiwan radio said the group was scheduled to return to Taiwan at around 3.00 p.m. (0700 GMT).
Ching's office declined to confirm or deny the trip, but said Ching had not been seen since Monday afternoon.
The agency said Ching decided to sail secretly to avoid publicity, which he said was the reason for a failed mission in May.
A flotilla of activists was driven away from the waters around the disputed islands by Japanese coast guards.
The archipelago is claimed by Taiwan, Japan and China.

The island chain has ignited fiery nationalist passions in Chinese communities in Hong Kong and Taiwan since a Japanese right-wing group built a makeshift lighthouse there in July 1996, a move they said bolstered Japan's sovereignty.
